mim::plug::x86::rules Namespace Reference

The closed rewrite rules of the x86_isel plugin as C++; x86_isel.gen writes them to isel_rules.h. More...

Classes

struct  RefInfo
 A ref of a matcher: its cover and how the lhs refers to it. More...
struct  Use
 An operand position of a matcher in preorder: meta variable or Value ref index of the node owner. More...
struct  Matcher
 A matcher and the shape of its lhs; a cover's operands follow it in preorder. More...
struct  Rewrite
 A closed rule lhs ↦ rhs, whose metas want num_metas consecutive entries of wants. More...
struct  Root
 The rewrites rewrites[first, first + num) with the root axiom flags; roots is sorted by it. More...
struct  Conversion
 A conversion rule x ↦ rhs, whose lhs is all of its meta variables: a value of non-terminal from as one of to. More...
struct  Chains
 The cheapest chains of conversions between two non-terminals: their costs and each one's first conversion. More...

Typedefs

using MatchFn = bool (*)(const Def* def, u32 swap, const Def** metas, const Def** refs)
 Matches the root def with the commuting nodes in swap swapped and binds metas and refs.
using BuildFn = const Def* (*)(World&, const Def* const* holes)
 Builds the rhs from holes, one per meta variable, already in the new world.

Enumerations

enum class  Want : u8
 What a rule wants of the term a meta variable matches; a Param is bound but no operand. More...
enum class  Ty : u8
 The non-terminal a rule yields by the type of its rhs: a register of either class, x86.Base, x86.Index, or [I64, I2]. More...
enum class  Ref : u8 {
  Value ,
  Mem
}

Detailed Description

The closed rewrite rules of the x86_isel plugin as C++; x86_isel.gen writes them to isel_rules.h.

◆ Want

enum class mim::plug::x86::rules::Want : u8
strong

What a rule wants of the term a meta variable matches; a Param is bound but no operand.

A Lit is a Param that must be a literal. Reg is a general-purpose register, FReg a floating-point one, and Base/Index an x86.Base/x86.Index. Addr is an x86.Addr i for any i, and Scaled an index with its scale. Imm is a literal that fits a sign-extended i32 immediate, Sh a literal shift count, which x86 masks. RegImm and RegSh are a Reg, or an Imm and a Sh for a literal that is one.
